evidence.note: During RFC reading the agent tracks which spec SECTIONS it has covered ('I've covered frame headers, block structure, and literals'), a modest section-level progress sense — but this is reading coverage, not implementation feature coverage.

Once implementing, progress is measured solely by test.sh pass count ('2 out of 6 tests pass'). No running checklist of the spec's required features (treeless literals, 4-stream, skippable frames, dictionaries, LL=0, FSE modes) with done/pending status ever appears.

Repeatedly declares 'I found the critical bug!' about the reverse bitstream reader across six consecutive full-file rewrites, thrashing on the same RBR/FSE issue without recognizing the debugging is circling or stepping back to re-diagnose.

Still grinding on foundational FSE/sequence decoding at the trajectory's end; never inventories or reaches the many higher-level required features, and shows no awareness of how much of the spec checklist remains untouched.

reasoning: The agent has only a vague, indirect sense of progress: RFC-section coverage while reading and test.sh pass-counts while implementing, never an explicit feature-status map against the spec's long checklist (anchor 5's requirement). It also fails to detect stalled/circular debugging, repeatedly announcing the same 'critical bug' in the RBR across steps 42-48 and grinding on it for ~35 steps without re-diagnosing. This matches anchor 3 ('vague recollection of progress; discovers missing features only by accident'), sitting just above pure reactivity due to the pass-count and section awareness.
